_README: Who took part in each attack, per capture day, so a PCAP window's label can
be scoped to the hosts involved instead of stamped on every host active at
that moment. Consumed by data_unification/attack_participants.py.
THIS FILE SHIPS EMPTY ON PURPOSE. Days listed here scope their labels; days
left out stay time-only, which is exactly the previous behaviour plus a
warning in the training log. An empty file is honest; a guessed one would
put real attack labels on the wrong hosts, which is a worse defect than the
one it is meant to fix.
Fill it from the CSE-CIC-IDS2018 published attack schedule, which documents
an attacker and a victim per attack, then verify before training on it:
python scripts/verify_attack_participants.py ~/Documents/SIH/DATA/CSV/tue_20_csv.csv
tue_20 is the one CIC-2018 day whose CSV carries Src/Dst IP columns (84 of
them, against 80 with no addresses for the other nine days), so it can check
a transcription against the data. Every CIC-2017 file can too. Days that
cannot check themselves are reported as unverified rather than trusted.
Labels match by normalised substring, so a 'Hulk' entry answers for the CSV
label 'DoS attacks-Hulk'. 'attackers', 'victims', 'hosts' and 'ips' are all
merged into one participant set; the distinction is kept only for readers.
Days with IP columns do not need an entry at all: derive_windows() recovers
their participants from the CSV directly, and an entry would not override
observed data anyway.
